questions.question:
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories. "The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling." Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity. She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery. She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996. Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking. She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential. Both people succeeded not "despite" adversity but thanks to it.
choices: ① What did Hans Andersen consider the sources of his popular stories?
② Which country did Aimee Mullins represent at the 1996 Paralympics?
③ What careers has Aimee Mullins pursued besides sports?
④ How does Aimee Mullins view her physical condition?
⑤ What made it possible for Andersen and Mullins to succeed?
questions.why: 1996년 패럴림픽에 '참가했다'는 내용만 있고, 어느 나라 대표였는지는 글에 없다.
questions.wrong: ① poverty·loss of his father·being disrespected, ③ modeling·acting·public speaking, ④ not a disability but … potential, ⑤ 마지막 문장 thanks to it(역경 덕분)에서 각각 답을 찾을 수 있다. not "despite" … but 구조를 거꾸로 읽지 않도록 주의.

questions.question:
Foldscope에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
Ultimately, Prakash and Cybulski settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, allowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. When crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder.
choices: ① 방수 판지와 작은 유리구슬 렌즈로 만들어졌다.
② 140배까지 확대해 혈액 세포와 세균을 관찰할 수 있다.
③ 무게가 8그램이고 외부 전원 없이 사용할 수 있다.
④ 휴대전화 카메라에 연결해야만 표본을 확대해 볼 수 있다.
⑤ 나이지리아에서 가짜 말라리아 치료제를 가려내는 데 쓰였다.
questions.why: 휴대전화 카메라와 호환되면 사진·영상을 남길 수 있어 쓸모가 '더 커진다(further enhanced)'고 했을 뿐, 연결해야만 볼 수 있다는 말은 없다.
questions.wrong: ① waterproof cardboard paper·glass ball lens, ② 140 times·blood cells·bacteria, ③ 8 grams·no external power source, ⑤ Nigeria·fake antimalarial drugs와 일치한다. '~해야만'처럼 조건을 바꾼 선지를 먼저 의심하자.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 표현의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash ①<u>came across</u> an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is ②<u>of minor importance</u> in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was ③<u>bulky and awkward to transport</u>, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers ④<u>felt nervous about</u> using it. A cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives. It was not until he met Jim Cybulski that his idea of an affordable and accessible microscope began to ⑤<u>take shape</u>.
questions.why: 말라리아로 매년 50만 명 이상이 사망하므로(so) 조기 진단은 '매우 중요하다(crucial)'가 되어야 한다. of minor importance는 정반대.
questions.wrong: ① 우연히 발견하다, ③ 부피가 크고 옮기기 어렵다, ④ 비싸고 섬세해서 긴장했다, ⑤ 구체화되다 — 모두 앞뒤 흐름과 맞다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] Once you have done so, return to the task you set aside a moment ago.

Second, have "me time," that is, personal time to look after yourself. Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future. ( ① ) Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise. ( ② ) If you don't know where to start, the STOP technique can be a great meditative technique. It works like this. ( ③ ) Stop whatever you are doing. Take a few deep breaths. ( ④ ) Observe your emotions and thoughts as they are, not judging them as good or bad. ( ⑤ ) Or start something different based on what you observed. Now go forward with your life.
questions.why: ⑤ 뒤의 Or start something different는 '하던 일로 돌아가거나, 또는 다른 일을 시작하라'의 뒷부분이다. 앞부분인 주어진 문장이 ⑤에 와야 Or가 이어진다. done so는 바로 앞 Observe를 가리킨다.
questions.wrong: ④에 넣으면 '하던 일로 돌아간' 뒤에 감정을 관찰하게 되어 S-T-O-P 순서가 무너진다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
A large part of what we see is what we expect to see. This explains why we "see" faces and figures in a flickering campfire, or in moving clouds. This is why Leonardo da Vinci advised artists to discover their motifs by staring at patches on a blank wall. A fire provides a constant flickering change in visual information that never integrates into anything solid and thereby allows the brain to engage in a play of hypotheses. On the other hand, the wall does not present us with very much in the way of visual clues, and so the brain begins to make more and more hypotheses and desperately searches for confirmation. A crack in the wall looks a little like the profile of a nose and suddenly a whole face appears, or a leaping horse, or a dancing figure. In cases like these the brain's visual strategies are projecting images from within the mind out onto the world.
choices: ① Perception Shaped More by Anticipation Than by Sight
② Leonardo da Vinci's Method for Discovering Artistic Motifs
③ How the Brain Integrates Flickering Visual Information
④ The Scarcity of Visual Clues in Ordinary Surroundings
⑤ Why Humans Misidentify Faces in Moving Clouds
questions.why: 첫 문장 '보는 것의 상당 부분은 보기를 기대하는 것'과 마지막 문장 '마음속 이미지를 바깥에 투사한다'를 합친 제목이다(expect → anticipation).
questions.wrong: ② 다빈치의 조언과 ④ 벽의 단서 부족은 예시일 뿐이다. ③ 불빛 정보는 '결코 하나로 합쳐지지 않는다(never integrates)'고 했다. ⑤는 구름 속 얼굴 하나로 범위를 좁혔다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
While the definition of honor may differ significantly depending on cultural context, the presence of the concept ①<u>itself</u> is nearly universal among human societies. Some sociologists maintain that honor evolved primarily to preserve social stability by encouraging cooperation. However, I find that a personal view of honor hits closer to home. As humans, we are aware that our lives are limited, and we must face the reality ②<u>which</u> we have only a short time to shape how others perceive us. Although the pursuit of wealth and status may offer temporary satisfaction during our lives, such achievements eventually lose their meaning once we are gone. What remains ③<u>is</u> the way we lived. The values we upheld, the honesty behind our choices, and the respect we showed to others often ④<u>become</u> the foundation of how we are remembered. To live honorably is not just about meeting society's expectations, but about creating a lasting image that reflects ⑤<u>who</u> we truly were.
questions.why: which 뒤 we have only a short time …는 빠진 성분이 없는 완전한 절이다. 따라서 the reality의 내용을 풀어 주는 동격의 that이 와야 한다.
questions.wrong: ① 강조 용법 재귀대명사(생략 가능), ③ What remains는 단수 취급, ④ 주어가 The values, the honesty, and the respect 세 개라 복수 become, ⑤ reflects의 목적어가 되는 의문사절 — 모두 맞다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
When people hear the term 'not-for-profit,' they often picture charitable organizations that depend primarily on donations and grants. This common view fosters the ①<u>well-founded</u> belief that not-for-profits cannot operate as self-sustaining enterprises. In reality, the legal definition of a nonprofit is far ②<u>broader</u> than mere charity. Such organizations are fully permitted to generate revenue, provided that those funds are channeled toward their stated mission or a social purpose. In recent years, many nonprofits have shown that they can ③<u>flourish</u> financially. The crucial distinction is that they are 'not-for-private-profit': no individual may personally benefit from the organization's earnings. While employees or contributors can be paid fairly for their work, profits cannot be ④<u>distributed</u> to shareholders or private individuals. Instead, a board or committee oversees financial decisions to ensure ⑤<u>transparency</u>. If the organization is dissolved, its remaining assets must be devoted to the public good and cannot be claimed by any single person.
questions.why: 바로 다음 문장이 In reality로 이 생각을 반박하므로, '근거 있는' 생각이 아니라 '잘못된(mistaken)' 생각이어야 한다.
questions.wrong: ② 법적 정의는 자선보다 넓다, ③ 재정적으로 번창할 수 있다, ④ 이익은 주주에게 분배될 수 없다, ⑤ 이사회가 투명성을 보장한다 — 모두 흐름에 맞다.

questions.question:
다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
Wu wei is a cornerstone of Taoist thought that instructs people when to act and when to hold back. Although the term literally means "without action," it should not be confused with indolence or mere passivity. Instead, it centers on harnessing the energy that already flows around us and converting it into a potent driving force. In the martial arts, seasoned practitioners learn to seize an opponent's momentum and turn it back against him with striking efficiency. Mastering this art of redirection makes people more formidable fighters, but it also enriches their ordinary lives, keeping them in balance with their surroundings and allowing them to approach routine tasks with greater ease. Those who practice wu wei, in this sense, <u>travel like boats that let the river's current do the rowing</u>. Attuned to this natural rhythm, they handle their tasks in proper sequence and attend successfully to everything that demands their attention.
choices: ① Retreating from action altogether is the surest path to inner peace.
② Defeating opponents requires overpowering them with greater force.
③ Letting nature take its course means abandoning every responsibility.
④ The flow of the Earth's energy can be measured and controlled precisely.
⑤ One accomplishes more by aligning with forces already in motion than by resisting them.
questions.why: 무위는 게으름이 아니라 이미 흐르는 에너지를 이용하는 것(harnessing the energy that already flows)이다. 강물이 노를 젓게 하는 배 = 이미 움직이는 힘에 맞추어 더 많은 것을 이룬다.
questions.wrong: ① 행동을 아예 멈추는 것, ③ 모든 책임을 버리는 것은 글이 부정한 '수동성'이다. ② 힘으로 제압하는 것은 반대 방향이고, ④ 에너지를 측정·통제한다는 말은 없다.

questions.question:
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
There has been a lot of discussion on why moths are attracted to light. The consensus seems to hold that moths are not so much attracted to lights as they are trapped by them, for the light becomes a sensory overload that disorients the insects and sends them into a holding pattern. ① A hypothesis called the Mach band theory suggests that moths see a dark area around a light source and head for it to escape the light. ② Another theory suggests that moths perceive the light coming from a source as a diffuse halo with a dark spot in the center. ③ The moths, attempting to escape the light, fly toward that imagined "portal," bringing them closer to the source. ④ Moths are also important nighttime pollinators, visiting many flowers that bloom only after dark. ⑤ As they approach the light, their reference point changes and they circle the light hopelessly trying to reach the portal.
questions.why: 글은 나방이 불빛에 '갇히는' 이유를 설명한다. ④의 꽃가루 매개는 같은 나방 이야기지만 이 주제에서 벗어난다. ④를 빼면 ③(포털로 날아감)과 ⑤(가까워지면 기준점이 바뀜)가 바로 이어진다.
questions.wrong: 같은 소재(나방)를 쓰고 also까지 붙어 있어 관련 있어 보이는 함정이다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
As certain practices are repeated over time and become widely shared, the values they carry are reinforced and passed on, and we say they have become 'institutionalized.' Sometimes this takes a formal shape: rules and procedures are written down, and specialized roles are created to make sure they are followed. Courts, parliaments, and police forces display this formal character. Many other institutions, however, work quite differently, and the kitchen of a fine restaurant is one of them. Young cooks are carefully trained in recipes and techniques, yet nobody hands them a manual on 'how to be a good cook' — how to respect an ingredient, when to cover for a teammate, why a plate is never sent out unless it is right. Much like a child learning how to play 'nicely,' the apprentice cook comes to understand the values built into the role not through written instruction but by ________.
choices: ① passing them down to the colleagues in the kitchen
② concealing them from the colleagues in the kitchen
③ recording them in rules for the colleagues in the kitchen
④ separating them from the colleagues in the kitchen
⑤ absorbing them from the colleagues in the kitchen
questions.why: 요리사는 매뉴얼이 아니라, 아이가 '사이좋게 노는 법'을 배우듯 주변 동료들에게서 가치를 '흡수해' 배운다.
questions.wrong: ③ 규칙으로 적어 두는 것은 법원·의회 같은 '공식' 제도화 방식이라 반대다. ①은 전달 방향이 거꾸로이고, ②④는 글과 무관하다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Whatever divides them, the scientist and the artist set out from a single puzzle: whether two minds can ________. The scientific inquirer hunts for those properties of an object that can be detached from personal impression — ideally, features that lend themselves to measurement and whose values therefore stay fixed regardless of who is looking. By this route, she arrives at a reality that exists apart from any observer. The artist, by contrast, depends on the force of her craft to forge a union between her own inner life and that of her audience. To a scientific mind, this may sound like wishful sorcery: you claim you can picture something so intensely that it will materialize in another person's head exactly as you conceive it? Yet the artist pursues precisely the reverse of the scientist's observer-free reality. She constructs a reality that relies on its beholders — indeed, one that cannot come into being at all unless people take part in it.
choices: ① completely eliminate subjectivity from every act of perception
② create a reality that exists independently of all observers
③ perceive one and the same thing in an identical manner
④ measure the properties of an object without any instruments
⑤ permanently separate artistic imagination from objective reality
questions.why: 과학자와 예술가의 공통 질문은 '두 사람이 같은 것을 같은 방식으로 볼 수 있는가'이다. 과학자는 관찰자와 무관한 실재로, 예술가는 관찰자에게 의존하는 실재로 답한다.
questions.wrong: ②는 과학자 쪽 답일 뿐 공통 질문이 아니다. ①⑤ completely·permanently 같은 극단어, ④ measurement를 비튼 선지다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] Simonides alone, however, could still picture the banquet table and recall the seat each guest had occupied.

According to an ancient legend, the Greek poet Simonides once narrowly escaped a deadly accident during a grand banquet. Shortly after reciting a poem, he was called outside by two unknown visitors. ( ① ) Moments later, the banquet hall collapsed, killing everyone inside. ( ② ) The bodies were so badly damaged that even the victims' families couldn't recognize them. ( ③ ) Using this mental image, he successfully helped identify the dead. ( ④ ) This experience led him to a powerful insight: memory becomes more effective when abstract ideas are connected to vivid images arranged in a specific order. ( ⑤ ) Concrete visuals are remembered with much greater ease than abstract notions, and structured sequences enhance recall more than random groups. This technique, later known as the method of loci, became the basis of classical memory training. Simonides's discovery shows how ancient thinkers intuitively grasped cognitive principles long before they were formally studied by modern science.
questions.why: ③ 뒤 this mental image(이 마음속 이미지)가 가리킬 대상이 주어진 문장의 picture the banquet table밖에 없다. however는 '가족도 알아보지 못했다'와 대조된다.
questions.wrong: ②에 넣으면 시신 상태를 말하기 전에 '그러나'가 나와 대조가 성립하지 않는다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Most shoppers assume that the more reviews they can read, the better their purchasing decisions will be. Online marketplaces seem to confirm this belief, displaying thousands of ratings and comments for nearly every product. When considering a costly purchase, people trust that a quick scroll through these opinions will reveal which option is truly reliable. Yet when the volume of feedback outstrips a buyer's capacity to weigh it, the outcome is often bewilderment rather than insight. Contradictory verdicts pile up, and a handful of fabricated or exaggerated posts can spread faster than careful, verified assessments. Shoppers then drift into separate camps, each loyal to the sources it happens to trust and dismissive of the rest. Rather than becoming wiser consumers, they may end up more fragmented and less able to agree on what is actually worth buying.

[요약문] Contrary to the belief that more reviews lead to wiser choices, opinions that __(A)__ a buyer's capacity to weigh them can leave shoppers confused and __(B)__ rather than better informed.
choices: ① exceed … divided
② support … divided
③ exceed … united
④ surpass … enlightened
⑤ match … misled
questions.why: 리뷰의 양이 판단 능력을 넘어서면(outstrips → exceed) 혼란이 생기고, 소비자들이 서로 다른 진영으로 갈라진다(separate camps, fragmented → divided).
questions.wrong: ③ united, ④ enlightened는 결론과 반대다. ②⑤ support·match는 '능력을 넘어선다'는 내용과 맞지 않는다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Museums have their origins, both materially and conceptually, in the collections of the wealthy and the privileged. Historically, they displayed the wealth of the collector, but also his cognitive power. The acquisition and display of beautiful, curious, or rare objects in the Renaissance ①<u>confirming</u> the collector's access to the secrets of the universe contained in those objects, ②<u>which</u> mediated between the visible and the invisible, the material world and the order that underlay ③<u>it</u>. The collection indexed its proprietor's access to this domain of hidden meaning and placed outsiders who ④<u>were</u> granted access to the collections in an inferior position. Paying their respects to the collection, they acknowledged the status of the collector. Although the evolution of the collection into the museum during the early modern period ⑤<u>occurs</u> along with a series of epistemic shifts in the structure of knowledge, museums remain fundamentally concerned with expressing the relationship of knowledge and ownership to identity, power, and status.
questions.why: 주어 The acquisition and display of … objects in the Renaissance가 길지만, 문장에 본동사가 없다. confirming → confirmed.
questions.wrong: ② 앞의 objects를 받는 계속적 용법, ③ it = the material world, ④ 선행사 outsiders가 복수, ⑤ 주어 the evolution이 단수 — 모두 맞다.

questions.question:
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
Because we live in uncertain times, how we deal with ambiguity matters more than ever. Many people feel uncomfortable when faced with unclear situations and immediately seek clear answers or concrete solutions, a tendency that often comes from educational systems that focus on finding a single answer. ① But according to psychological studies, individuals who learn to embrace uncertainty have remarkable advantages in creative problem-solving tasks. ② When confronted with unclear scenarios, these people resist the urge to jump to conclusions. ③ Still, in most situations, settling quickly on a single clear answer is what allows people to perform at their best. ④ Instead, they allow themselves to sit with the discomfort of not knowing. ⑤ This helps them gather more information, consider new approaches, and discover creative connections between seemingly unrelated concepts.
questions.why: 글은 '모호함을 견디는 사람이 창의적 문제 해결에 유리하다'는 주장이다. ③만 '빨리 하나의 답을 정하는 것이 낫다'는 반대 주장이다.
questions.wrong: ③을 빼면 ②의 resist the urge(서두르지 않는다)와 ④의 Instead(대신 모름을 견딘다)가 바로 이어진다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] Online video-sharing services, on the other hand, rewrote the very rules by which audiences relate to the screen.

Let's explore how HDTV and online video sharing platforms altered the core ways audiences engage with their respective forms of media. The transition from analog television to HDTV represents a shift in degree rather than in kind. ( ① ) With HDTV, there are more pixels, the sound quality is more immersive, and the colors appear more vivid. ( ② ) However, the way people consume content remains unchanged. ( ③ ) Viewers still select a channel and watch passively, just as they did with traditional analog broadcasts. ( ④ ) They turned watching videos on the web into a mainstream activity. ( ⑤ ) They also allowed users to upload their own clips, rate or recommend others, and participate in discussions around the content, which moved them far beyond the passive viewing model of conventional television. By typing just a few keys, users could embed a clip from one website onto their own. This technology empowered everyday enthusiasts to effectively create personalized television networks by curating and combining videos from all over the world.
questions.why: ④ 뒤 They turned watching videos on the web …의 They는 앞 문장의 Viewers로는 뜻이 맞지 않는다. 주어진 문장의 services를 받아야 한다. on the other hand는 '여전히 수동적으로 본다'와 대조된다.
questions.wrong: ⑤ 뒤 They also도 services를 받으므로, 주어진 문장은 그보다 앞인 ④에 와야 한다.

questions.question:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
When a painter borrows rhythm, a notion native to music, to describe what a canvas must contain, the borrowing is never innocent: it signals an art straining against the borders nature drew for it.

(A) Composition, after all, has long been the native tongue of the spatial arts, from the cathedral to the carved figure to the framed canvas. To compose is to set the elements of an image in such relation that their relative scale, form, hue, and brightness give the eye a sense of balance.

(B) Rhythm does not discard that older idea; it absorbs it and then adds something painting had never claimed — a pattern that returns at regular intervals across the passage of time. So once a spatial arrangement is taken in by the viewer as a sequence unfolding moment by moment, composition itself turns into rhythm.

(C) Why, then, did Picasso, Braque, and Gris insist on layering this musical term over the familiar one? The motive is less puzzling than it first appears.
questions.why: (A) 공간 예술의 기본 개념은 구성(composition) → (C) 왜 화가들은 '익숙한 것(구성)' 위에 이 음악 용어(리듬)를 덧붙였나 → (B) 리듬은 구성을 품고 시간 속 반복을 더한다.
questions.wrong: (C)의 the familiar one과 (B)의 that older idea는 모두 composition을 가리키므로 (A)가 맨 앞이어야 한다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
In engineering, a design improves by eliminating alternatives: each revision tightens tolerances and edges closer to the single solution that works best. Literary interpretation moves in the opposite direction. A great novel does not become clearer because critics agree on one correct reading; its value grows as readers generate an ever wider array of readings, each illuminating a facet the others had missed. A new interpretation therefore earns its place not by settling which earlier reading was right, but by exposing how narrow and provisional those readings were. To an outsider expecting the steady convergence of a laboratory, the history of criticism may look like a widening fog — a field that seems to unsettle conclusions it had already reached. Yet for literature, this apparent disorder is the very sign of progress, since understanding a rich text means ________.
choices: ① converging on the single reading the author intended
② multiplying the vantage points from which it can be viewed
③ eliminating interpretations that lack textual evidence
④ approximating the truth through ever greater precision
⑤ permanently resolving the disputes among earlier critics
questions.why: 공학은 대안을 줄여 하나의 답으로 가지만, 문학 해석은 읽기를 계속 늘려 가는 것이 발전이다. 따라서 풍부한 텍스트를 이해한다는 것은 '바라보는 관점을 늘리는 것'이다.
questions.wrong: ①③④는 공학(과학)식 '좁히기'다. ⑤는 permanently라는 극단어에 내용도 반대다.

questions.question:
다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
When recorded music moved from magnetic tape to strings of numbers, the change reached far beyond sound quality. Translating a performance into data meant that any alteration could be taken back: a producer could stretch, bend, or reshape a phrase while the untouched original waited safely in the background. In effect, <u>the studio traded its chisel for a pencil with an eraser</u>. A slip that once might have ruined an afternoon's work became a trivial matter, and producers grew bolder, trying out ideas they would never have risked before. Editing changed in the same spirit. Where engineers had once sliced tape with razor blades and joined the pieces by hand, they now dragged a cursor across a screen, rewriting the instructions that described the sound. Because those instructions could be adjusted down to the thousandth of a second, joins could be hidden so perfectly that no listener would notice — or exaggerated deliberately to create textures no one had heard before.
choices: ① Digital tools forced musicians to abandon their original recordings entirely.
② Changes became reversible, so mistakes no longer carried serious costs.
③ Producers had to plan every sound precisely before recording it.
④ Physical editing with blades remained more accurate than computer editing.
⑤ Sound quality improved so much that editing became unnecessary.
questions.why: 밑줄 앞 '어떤 변경도 되돌릴 수 있었다'와 뒤 '실수가 사소한 일이 되었다'가 근거다. 끌(되돌릴 수 없음) → 지우개 달린 연필(되돌릴 수 있음).
questions.wrong: ① 원본은 안전하게 남아 있었다. ③ 오히려 마음껏 실험했다. ④ 면도날 편집은 과거 방식일 뿐 더 정확하다는 말은 없다. ⑤ 첫 문장은 '음질을 넘어선 변화'라고 했다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Organizations celebrate employees who 'think outside the box,' treating the phrase as a passport to insight and innovation. Yet the praise often rests on a shallow reading of the idea. Consider a nineteenth-century carriage maker who refused to copy his rivals. He lightened the frames, softened the springs, and painted the doors in colors no one had dared to use, and his carriages sold well. By every ordinary measure, he had stepped outside the box. But each of his bold departures still answered the same unspoken question — how to build a better carriage — and so his imagination never wandered beyond the horse that pulled it. Leaping out of one container, it turns out, frequently lands us in a larger one whose walls we fail to notice. Genuine reinvention, then, depends less on escaping the box than on ________, for only then can the carriage maker ask whether people need a carriage at all.
choices: ① decorating the box more boldly than one's competitors
② copying the boxes that rivals have already escaped
③ refining the box until it can no longer be improved
④ questioning the assumptions that built the box in the first place
⑤ completely ignoring the customers who rely on the box
questions.why: 마차 제작자는 상자 밖으로 나간 것 같지만 '더 나은 마차'라는 질문 안에 머물렀다. 진짜 혁신은 그 상자를 만든 전제 자체(사람들에게 마차가 필요한가)를 묻는 데서 나온다.
questions.wrong: ① 더 과감한 장식, ③ 상자 안에서의 개선은 글이 '얕은 이해'라고 한 것이다. ② copy는 글과 반대, ⑤는 극단어 선지다.

questions.question:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
It is widely taken for granted that many hands make light work and that a team will outperform the same people laboring alone. The Ringelmann effect casts doubt on this comfortable assumption. It describes a curious tendency: people (A) [withhold / redouble] effort when their contribution is blended into a group's, a pattern that can quietly erode performance on sports teams, in classroom projects, and across the workplace. The idea is named after Maximilien Ringelmann, a French engineer who asked volunteers to haul on a rope while he gauged the force each one applied. As more pullers took hold, the combined force rose far less than the sum of their solo efforts would predict — in a crowd of shoulders, effort quietly slips beneath the surface. Psychologists now call this social loafing, and it leaves the group's output (B) [higher / lower] than managers tend to expect. Recognizing it is the first step: teams that make each member's share (C) [visible / anonymous] are far more likely to sustain equal participation and steady output.
choices: ① redouble … higher … visible
② redouble … lower … anonymous
③ withhold … higher … anonymous
④ withhold … lower … anonymous
⑤ withhold … lower … visible
questions.why: (A) 뒤에 '성과를 갉아먹는다'가 이어지므로 노력을 덜 들인다(withhold). (B) 합친 힘이 기대치에 못 미쳤으므로 결과가 더 낮다(lower). (C) 태만은 개인 몫이 묻힐 때 생기므로, 각자의 몫을 드러내야(visible) 참여가 유지된다.
questions.wrong: ④는 (A)(B)는 맞지만 (C)에서 '익명'을 골라 반대가 된다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] In reality, however, a handful of large publishing houses stand at the library's doors like toll collectors.

Science advances on a foundation of trust: a finding counts only if others can repeat it and arrive at the same result. ( ① ) Objectivity therefore demands that every observation, experiment, and theoretical model pass an independent inspection before it is admitted into print. ( ② ) A new result must first be laid out and defended in a written article, which qualified peers then examine, test, and, where necessary, repair. ( ③ ) Only after surviving this gauntlet is a discovery stamped as official and shelved in the vast common library of scientific knowledge, a library built brick by brick across generations. ( ④ ) Because science is a collective and universal enterprise, every researcher ought to be able to walk freely through its aisles without delay. ( ⑤ ) Their tolls, known as paywalls, lock most peer-reviewed journals behind turnstiles that many cannot afford to pass. Since it is largely taxpayers' money that funds research around the globe, the fruits of that research should be open to anyone, anywhere.
questions.why: ⑤ 뒤 Their tolls(그들의 통행료)의 Their가 가리킬 대상이 주어진 문장의 toll collectors밖에 없다. however는 '누구나 자유롭게 드나들어야 한다'는 이상과 현실을 대조한다.
questions.wrong: ④에 넣으면 '현실'을 말한 뒤에 다시 '이상'이 나와 흐름이 거꾸로 된다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
For generations, foresters believed that a tree grew best when its rivals were cleared away, giving it unchallenged access to light, water, and soil. Recent research paints a different picture. In an undisturbed woodland, neighboring trees are linked below ground, and through these links nutrients and water are distributed so that each member reaches its full potential. Remove the so-called competitors, and the survivors are left isolated, sending signals into soil that now holds only stumps. Freed from their neighbors, a few trees surge ahead, photosynthesizing at a furious pace and thickening rapidly — yet such sprinters rarely live long. Others, deprived of the support they once drew from stronger companions, weaken and soon succumb to insects and fungi. A growing number of forest managers have therefore begun to leave the crowded stands alone, judging the strength of a woodland not by its tallest individuals but by the web that holds them together.

[요약문] Clearing away a tree's neighbors may seem helpful, but because trees __(A)__ resources through underground links, foresters are increasingly __(B)__ dense stands rather than thinning them.
choices: ① contest … preserving
② share … clearing
③ share … preserving
④ hoard … thinning
⑤ exchange … harvesting
questions.why: 나무들은 땅속 연결로 양분과 물을 나눈다(distributed → share). 그래서 숲 관리자들은 빽빽한 숲을 그대로 둔다(leave alone → preserving).
questions.wrong: ① contest는 '경쟁' 틀로 읽은 오답, ②④⑤의 clearing·thinning·harvesting은 나무를 베어 내는 쪽이라 결론과 반대다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Every economic exchange is, at heart, a social encounter. When barter gave way to coins, the shift altered not just how goods changed hands but how people stood in relation to one another. A hand-carved tool or a string of shells carried the fingerprints of its maker; it was a story as much as a payment. Money, by contrast, is a colorless ruler that can be cut into exact units, letting us size up goods and services with mathematical neatness. Like a solvent, it dissolves the particular textures of things into a single, uniform liquid of price. The habit of mind it trains — cool, calculating, and precise — does not stay politely inside the marketplace. It seeps into rooms that once had no price tags at all. Today even the bonds of family and the pleasure of a painting are increasingly ________.
choices: ① weighed on scales built for quantities rather than qualities
② protected from the logic that governs the marketplace
③ cherished as stories that carry the fingerprints of their makers
④ completely freed from the habit of calculation
⑤ exchanged through barter instead of coins
questions.why: 돈은 모든 것을 가격이라는 하나의 단위로 녹인다. 그 계산적 사고가 가족과 예술에까지 스며들어, 이제는 질이 아니라 양으로 평가된다.
questions.wrong: ③⑤는 돈 이전(물물교환) 시대의 모습이다. ②④는 '시장 논리가 스며든다'는 결론과 반대다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
The rise of digital platforms has made us far more guarded about what we reveal online. Students and job seekers comb through their profiles, aware that admissions officers and employers may be looking. Yet this instinct to put our best foot forward is not confined to screens; it shapes our conduct in the physical world as well. Researchers at a British university once examined campus security records to identify the three spots where bicycles were most often stolen. Rather than adding guards or cameras, they simply hung large posters showing a pair of staring eyes above the words 'We Are Watching You.' Thefts at those spots dropped sharply, while they rose elsewhere on campus. Notably, the posters were mere paper: no one was actually monitoring the racks. What restrained the would-be thieves, then, was not ________, but the mere impression of being observed.
choices: ① the heightened visibility of their online profiles
② the deterrent effect of additional security personnel
③ any actual likelihood of detection
④ a sudden scarcity of unattended bicycles
⑤ the formal penalties displayed beneath the eyes
questions.why: 포스터는 종이일 뿐 아무도 실제로 감시하지 않았다(no one was actually monitoring). 도둑을 막은 것은 실제로 들킬 가능성이 아니라 '보이고 있다는 느낌'이었다.
questions.wrong: ② 경비를 늘리지 않았다(Rather than adding guards). ⑤ 포스터에는 처벌 문구가 없었다. ①은 첫 부분의 온라인 이야기다.

questions.question:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
Much of what lets us move smoothly through an ordinary day is a quiet bet on what will probably happen next; having rehearsed the few likeliest scenarios, we are spared from working things out in the middle of them.

(A) The same economy governs the objects in our hands. Picture having to weigh, every single time, each conceivable function of every tool within reach — should the stapler or the frying pan drive this tack into the wall? A mind that refused to settle on the obvious use would stall before finishing a single chore.

(B) Seen this way, the tendency to treat an object as good for only its customary purpose deserves gratitude rather than scorn. It narrows our vision, admittedly, yet that very narrowing is what keeps us a step ahead of the world instead of a step behind it.

(C) At a café, no one is startled when the barista hands over a cup with a lid, nor wonders whether the steam rising from it signals danger. Leaving with a full stomach, no one stops to investigate why the hunger has gone. Because all of this was anticipated, none of it registers as a problem to be solved.
questions.why: 주어진 글(예측 덕분에 일상이 편하다) → (C) 카페 예시: 예상된 일은 문제가 되지 않는다 → (A) 같은 원리가 물건 사용에도 적용된다 → (B) 물건을 익숙한 용도로만 보는 경향은 오히려 고마운 것이다.
questions.wrong: (A)의 The same economy는 앞에 예시가 먼저 나와야 '같은' 원리가 된다. (B)의 object 이야기는 (A) 다음에 와야 자연스럽다.

questions.passage: Picture a fleet that has crossed the same waters for decades, its charts drawn from years of calm, predictable seas. One morning a storm that no chart had (a) <u>foreseen</u> rises out of nowhere, and even the largest vessels go down. The global economy met such a storm in 2008: the financial collapse was so abrupt and violent that the economists at the helm never saw it on the horizon, for their instruments, calibrated on historical patterns and rational assumptions, could read only weather they had already met. Rare, extreme events of this kind, which seem (b) <u>obvious</u> only in hindsight, are known as Black Swans. The idea questions whether the past can serve as a compass for the future, warning that the waves that reshape the world tend to rise from unexpected depths. The name itself was born in the 17th century, when Europeans, convinced that every swan was white, reached Australia and saw black ones; a single sighting (c) <u>shattered</u> a belief held for centuries. Events like these (d) <u>reinforce</u> our common assumptions, forcing institutions and individuals to redraw the way they chart risk and uncertainty. In the end, those who (e) <u>prepare</u> for storms they cannot yet name are the ones most likely to stay afloat.

questions.question: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: ① How Economists Predicted the 2008 Financial Crisis
② Why Charts of the Past Cannot Foresee Black Swans
③ The Discovery of Black Swans in 17th-Century Australia
④ Historical Patterns as a Reliable Compass for the Future
⑤ The Power of Rational Assumptions in Measuring Risk
questions.why: 과거 자료로 만든 '지도'로는 예측하지 못한 극단적 사건(블랙 스완)을 내다볼 수 없다는 글이다.
questions.wrong: ① 경제학자들은 2008년 위기를 예측하지 못했다. ④⑤ 과거 패턴·합리적 가정은 믿을 만한 나침반이 아니라고 했다. ③ 이름의 유래는 일부 예시일 뿐이다.

questions.question: 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: ① (a)
② (b)
③ (c)
④ (d)
⑤ (e)
questions.why: (d) 뒤에 '위험을 판단하는 방식을 다시 그리게 만든다'가 이어지므로, 이런 사건은 통념을 강화하는 것이 아니라 '뒤흔든다(challenge)'.
questions.wrong: (a) 어떤 지도도 예측하지 못한 폭풍, (b) 지나고 나서야 분명해 보인다, (c) 한 번의 목격이 믿음을 깨뜨렸다, (e) 이름 붙일 수 없는 폭풍에 대비하는 사람 — 모두 흐름에 맞다.
